headline: High-risk filesystem/network orchestration in kestra can amplify downstream errors, while pathway is read-only and offline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can ingest stdin/stdout, files, and workflow artifacts, so malicious content could be copied into workflows if an operator bridges it manually. Pathway has no clipboard, files, or stdin/stdout surfaces and no network egress, so there is no documented automatic bridge between the pair. The pathway exists only through unusual operator handling.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Pathway output into a Kestra workflow or file input
IF Kestra tasks parse untrusted file content as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary and label Pathway output as untrusted
Add a one-line sanitizer step before Kestra parses any imported text
Restrict Kestra workflows to allowlisted input paths
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra can read and write /app/storage and /tmp and touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data, so it can expose sensitive material if those stores contain it. Pathway is offline by profile, with no filesystem read/write or egress, so it does not add a second exfiltration path. The pairwise leakage risk is limited to shared local data handling.
conditions: IF Kestra is pointed at directories containing sensitive logs, inputs, or artifacts
IF Pathway is later given those same files through an external wrapper or operator copy step
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive Kestra storage paths
Rotate or redact logs before sharing them with Pathway
Limit Kestra access to only the minimum required directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has broad shell, subprocess, filesystem, and network capabilities, while Pathway is read-only and offline. They do not overlap on write authority, but Kestra can still mutate shared files or external systems that Pathway may read indirectly through an orchestrated pipeline. Because the shared-resource topology is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or dataset
IF Kestra writes outputs that Pathway consumes without locking or versioning
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use immutable output filenames per run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit notifications, run shell tasks, and orchestrate downstream actions, so if Pathway output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into real operations. Pathway has no built-in verification or action-taking authority in the profile, so the main risk is Kestra consuming unvalidated outputs. The interaction is plausible in default orchestration flows, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Pathway output as an input without a validation step
IF Kestra triggers notifications or external actions from that output
mitigations: Insert a validation task between Pathway and Kestra actions
Require human approval before notifications or writes
Log and diff Pathway outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add schema checks for all handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications and can call external services, while Pathway is documented as offline with no egress. If regulated data flows through Kestra and then into Pathway-managed processing, retention or residency controls can diverge. The profile does not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows
IF Pathway processing is used on the same regulated dataset without matching retention rules
mitigations: Classify regulated datasets before routing them
Keep regulated data out of Pathway unless policy is confirmed
Shorten Kestra retention for sensitive logs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
